sources.title: Handling Update Conflicts — PowerSync
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no immutable docs commit or client SDK release is specified by this page.
sources.locator: Lines 127–144: upload queue is ordered and sequentially drained to developer-configured backend; simplest backend uses per-field LWW/delete-wins; operations must be idempotent; a per-client incrementing operation ID is available for deduplication.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the official PowerSync conflict-handling page.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: PowerSync leaves backend conflict semantics to the app. The simple handler applies delete-wins and per-field last-write-wins; custom behavior and server validations are possible. Duplicate operation delivery is explicitly anticipated.
sources.applicability: Supports conditional analysis of the draft's LWW rejection, custom backend boundary, idempotency and command/transport identity distinction. Does not establish that all PowerSync SDKs group a multi-row business command atomically.

sources.title: Custom Conflict Resolution — PowerSync
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; page's React/Web and Node/Postgres examples are illustrative, not a pinned SDK release.
sources.locator: Lines 201–219 (local SQLite, queued upload and backend flow); 228–292 (CrudEntry, optional transactionId, complete-after-response example and duplicate handling); 308–310 and 382–391 (clock drift and sequence-number tradeoff); 569–654 (business-rule validation example); 853–855 (change-level pending/applied/failed states).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official page and inspected the upload, conflict/version, business-validation and status-tracking sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The sample calls transaction.complete() after the HTTP request returns; the documentation also warns that duplicate operations may occur. A CRUD transactionId is optional in its example. The page demonstrates patterns, not a universal SDK guarantee or roster domain behavior.
sources.applicability: Supports the implementation clarification that a durable rejected proposal and local queue terminalization must be coordinated and tested for the selected SDK. Supports distinguishing command identity from CRUD identity and preserving versioned alternatives to timestamps.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation — Constraints
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 official documentation, version path pinned.
sources.locator: §5.5 lines 92–101 (CHECK null/cross-row and immutability caveats); §5.5.6 lines 377–387 (EXCLUDE semantics).
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the PostgreSQL 18 constraints documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CHECK constraints cannot guarantee conditions over other rows/tables; UNIQUE, EXCLUDE, or FOREIGN KEY are suggested where applicable. EXCLUDE enforces only the declared operators over specified columns/expressions; schema/operator/index design matters.
sources.applicability: Confirms the draft's cross-row limitation and its caveat that interval exclusion is conditional and incomplete for qualification/dependency rules.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation — SET TRANSACTION
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 official documentation, version path pinned.
sources.locator: Lines 38–53: READ COMMITTED default; SERIALIZABLE visibility and serialization_failure rollback; isolation level must be set before first query/write.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the PostgreSQL 18 transaction documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: SERIALIZABLE detects concurrent patterns that cannot correspond to serial execution by aborting one transaction; callers need retry behavior. It does not itself supply roster rules.
sources.applicability: Confirms the draft correctly treats serializable transactions as a candidate mechanism with application retry handling, not as a complete business validator.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation — Row Security Policies
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 official documentation, version path pinned.
sources.locator: §5.9 lines 20–27: policies absent by default; after enablement no policy means default-deny; table owner normally bypasses; superuser/BYPASSRLS always bypass.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read PostgreSQL 18 row-security documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: RLS is not enabled by default. Policy default-deny applies only after enablement. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY can subject table owners; superusers and BYPASSRLS always bypass.
sources.applicability: Confirms the investigator's statement and supports keeping database role testing separate from sync filtering and application authorization.
